On bSSFP cines blood is bright; turbulent, high-velocity flows (stenoses, regurgitations) cause a signal void (dephasing jet). A systolic jet starting from the aortic valve and opening into the ascending aorta indicates aortic stenosis (or outflow obstruction), but its extent does not measure severity.
Severity is quantified with: Doppler echocardiography (peak velocity ≥ 4 m/s, mean gradient ≥ 40 mmHg, area < 1 cm² = severe) or MRI with phase-contrast on the plane just above the valve and planimetry of the valve area on an en face cine.
The left ventricle responds to pressure overload with concentric hypertrophy; MRI measures volumes, ejection fraction and mass (by contouring endocardium and epicardium on the short-axis stack at end-diastole and end-systole) and, with gadolinium, fibrosis (LGE), which worsens the prognosis.
Cine bSSFP: un vuoto di segnale sistolic: bSSFP cine: a systolic signal void beyond the aortic valve = turbulent flow; severity is given by velocity and area, not by the jet.
